n: The Lord told the brother of Jared to come down and write what he saw, but it was not to be revealed until after Christ’s crucifixion. King Mosiah kept these records hidden until Christ appeared to the Nephites.

f.w: king Mosiah
f.g: Mosiah II translated the Jaredite plates with interpreters.

f.w: lifted up upon the cross

n: After Christ visited the Nephites, he commanded that these things be made known.

f.w: made manifest

n: But the Nephites later fell into unbelief, and only the Lamanites remain, who reject the gospel. So Moroni is commanded to hide the records in the earth again.
Moroni has written on his plates the very things the brother of Jared saw — the greatest revelations ever given. This is the sealed portion of the gold plates.

f.w: there never were greater things made manifest

n: The Lord commanded Moroni to write and seal these things and to seal up the interpreters too. This is why part of the gold plates was sealed when Joseph Smith received them.

f.w: sealed up the interpreters

n: These sealed revelations will not go to the Gentiles until they repent and become clean before the Lord.
When people exercise faith like the brother of Jared and become sanctified, Christ will reveal what he saw and unfold all his revelations. Greater light depends on greater faith.

f.w: even as the brother of Jared did
sanctified
the Father of the heavens and of the earth

n: Christ declares that those who fight against or deny his word will be cursed and shown no greater things.

f.w: accursed
unto them will I show no greater things

n: At his command the heavens open and shut, the earth shakes, and people pass away as by fire. Christ is the Lord of all creation.

f.w: the heavens are opened and are shut

n: Whoever rejects Christ’s words rejects his disciples. If you doubt that Christ is speaking, judge for yourself — you will know at the last day.

f.w: judge ye

n: Those who believe will be visited by the Spirit and come to know these things are true and bear witness. The Spirit persuades people to do good.

f.w: manifestations of my Spirit
it persuadeth men to do good

n: Whatever persuades to do good comes from Christ, the source of all good. Rejecting his words is rejecting him and the Father who sent him. He is the light, life, and truth of the world.

f.w: whatsoever thing persuadeth men to do good is of me
the light, and the life, and the truth of the world

n: Christ invites the Gentiles to come to him and receive the “greater things” — knowledge hidden only because of unbelief.

f.w: Come unto me

n: He invites Israel too, promising to reveal the great things the Father prepared for them from the beginning, withheld only because of unbelief.

f.w: from the foundation of the world

n: When they tear away the “veil of unbelief” that keeps them in wickedness, hard hearts, and blind minds, and pray to the Father in Christ’s name with broken hearts, they will see that God remembers his covenant.

f.w: rend that veil of unbelief
a broken heart and a contrite spirit

n: Then the revelations given to John (the book of Revelation) will be opened to all. Seeing these things shows that the time is near.

f.w: my servant John

n: When you receive this record, know that the Father’s work has begun across the land. The Book of Mormon itself signals the latter-day gathering.

f.w: the work of the Father has commenced

n: Christ calls the whole earth to repent, believe his gospel, and be baptized. Believers who are baptized will be saved, unbelievers condemned, and signs will follow believers.

f.w: he that believeth and is baptized shall be saved

n: Blessed is the one faithful to Christ’s name at the last day; he will be lifted up into the kingdom prepared for him from the beginning. Christ seals the message with his own word.

f.w: the kingdom prepared for him
